Title: Moon Over the Jade Pavilion
Genres: Drama, Romance, Historical, Slice of Life
Tags: Archivists, Beautiful Female Lead, Calm Protagonist, Court Politics, Hidden Identity, Imperial Harem, Letters, Palace Intrigue, Slow Romance, Rainy Days, Mature Protagonist, Royalty, Secret Relationship, Second Chance, Tragic Past, Wise Protagonist, Clever Protagonist, Doting Love Interests, Heartwarming, Loneliness, Older Love Interests, Poetry, Gardens, Strategists, Tea Ceremony
Description:
For three seasons the archivist Wen Shu had catalogued the Jade Pavilion without once being noticed, which suited her perfectly.
Then she opened a letter that had been sealed for twenty years, and the quiet prince who lived in the east wing began appearing at her desk every evening with tea she had not asked for.
He said he only wanted the letter back.
He did not explain why he kept staying after she returned it, or why the palace guards had started to call her "the prince's scholar".
When the old Empress Dowager summoned her to the inner court, Wen Shu realised the letter had never been about love at all, but about a debt the whole dynasty would rather forget.
The prince, who had always been calm, lost his composure only once: the night she did not come back from the inner court. He walked through the rain to every gate of the palace until he found her, and said nothing at all on the way home.
Later the court would whisper about it for years.
